arxiv-2102-07862.title: Unified Shapley Framework to Explain Prediction Drift
arxiv-2102-07862.creator: Aalok Shanbhag, Avijit Ghosh, Josh Rubin
arxiv-2102-07862.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Aalok Shanbhag, Avijit Ghosh, Josh Rubin. Predictions are the currency of a machine learning model, and to understand the model’s behavior over segments of a dataset, or over time, is an important problem in machine learning research and practice. There currently is no systematic framework to understand this drift in prediction distributions over time or between two semantically meaningful slices of data, in terms of the input features and points.

arxiv-2104-05901.title: SRR-Net: A Super-Resolution-Involved Reconstruction Method for High Resolution MR Imaging
arxiv-2104-05901.creator: Wenqi Huang, Sen Jia, Ziwen Ke, Zhuo-Xu Cui, Jing Cheng, Yanjie Zhu, Dong Liang (🖂)
arxiv-2104-05901.description: Abstract Improving the image resolution and acquisition speed of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is a challenging problem. There are mainly two strategies dealing with the speed-resolution trade-off: (1) k k -space undersampling with high-resolution acquisition, and (2) a pipeline of lower resolution image reconstruction and image super-resolution.

arxiv-2109-04925.title: Rapid Model Architecture Adaption for Meta-Learning
arxiv-2109-04925.creator: Yiren Zhao, Xitong Gao, Ilia Shumailov, Nicolo Fusi, Robert Mullins
arxiv-2109-04925.description: Abstract Network Architecture Search (NAS) methods have recently gathered much attention. They design networks with better performance and use a much shorter search time compared to traditional manual tuning. Despite their efficiency in model deployments, most NAS algorithms target a single task on a fixed hardware system.

arxiv-2110-03513.title: Accelerated Componentwise Gradient Boosting using Efficient Data Representation and Momentum-based Optimization
arxiv-2110-03513.creator: Daniel Schalk, Bernd Bischl, David Rügamer
arxiv-2110-03513.description: Abstract Componentwise boosting (CWB), also known as model-based boosting, is a variant of gradient boosting that builds on additive models as base learners to ensure interpretability. CWB is thus often used in research areas where models are employed as tools to explain relationships in data. One downside of CWB is its computational complexity in terms of memory and runtime.

arxiv-2410-09147.title: A Candidate High-Velocity Exoplanet System in the Galactic Bulge
arxiv-2410-09147.creator: Sean K. Terry, Jean-Philippe Beaulieu, David P. Bennett, Aparna Bhattacharya, Jon Hulberg, Macy J. Huston, Naoki Koshimoto, Joshua W. Blackman, Ian A. Bond, Andrew A. Cole, Jessica R. Lu, Clément Ranc, Natalia E. Rektsini, Aikaterini Vandorou
arxiv-2410-09147.description: Abstract We present an analysis of adaptive optics (AO) images from the Keck-I telescope of the microlensing event MOA-2011-BLG-262. The original discovery paper by [ 13 ] reports two distinct possibilities for the lens system; a nearby gas giant lens with an exomoon companion or a very low mass star with a planetary companion in the galactic bulge.

arxiv-2503-22017.creator: Jianping Zeng 1 Shuyi Pei 1 Da Zhang 1 Yuchen Zhou 2 Amir Beygi 1 Xuebin Yao 1 Ramdas Kachare 1 Tong Zhang 1 Zongwang Li 1 Marie Nguyen 1 Rekha Pitchumani 1 Yang Soek Ki 1 Changhee Jung 2

arxiv-2505-04749.title: Abstract isomorphisms of isotropic root graded groups over rings. Thanks: The paper is written as part of the author’s post-doctoral fellowship at Bar-Ilan University, Department of Mathematics; and is supported by the ISF grant 1994/20.
arxiv-2505-04749.creator: Pavel Gvozdevsky
arxiv-2505-04749.description: Abstract . The celebrated Borel–Tits theorem provides a classification of abstract isomorphisms between (simple) isotropic groups over fields, showing that such isomorphisms arise from field isomorphisms and group-scheme isomorphisms. In this work, we extend the scope of this classification to certain class of group schemes over arbitrary commutative rings.

arxiv-2601-03862.title: Majorum : Ebb-and-Flow Consensus with Dynamic Quorums
arxiv-2601-03862.creator: Francesco D’Amato, Roberto Saltini, Thanh-Hai Tran, Yann Vonlanthen, Luca Zanolini
arxiv-2601-03862.description: Abstract Dynamic availability is the ability of a consensus protocol to remain live despite honest participants going offline and later rejoining. A well-known limitation is that dynamically available protocols, on their own, cannot provide strong safety guarantees during network partitions or extended asynchrony.

openalex-w2018743597.title: Functional Convergence of Neurons Generated in the Developing and Adult Hippocampus
openalex-w2018743597.creator: Diego Andrés Laplagne, Maria Soledad Esposito, Verónica C. Piatti, Nicolás A. Morgenstern, Chunmei Zhao, Henriette van Praag, Fred H. Gage, Alejandro Fabián Schinder
openalex-w2018743597.description: The dentate gyrus of the hippocampus contains neural progenitor cells (NPCs) that generate neurons throughout life. Developing neurons of the adult hippocampus have been described in depth. However, little is known about their functional properties as they become fully mature...

pmc-10573551.title: Blood Compatibility of Drug–Inorganic Hybrid in Human Blood: Red Blood Cell Hitchhiking and Soft Protein Corona
pmc-10573551.creator: Jing Xie, Hyoung-Mi Kim, Kai Kamada, Jae-Min Oh, Pedro Fonte
pmc-10573551.description: A drug-delivery system consisting of an inorganic host—layered double hydroxide (LDH)—and an anticancer drug—methotrexate (MTX)—was prepared via the intercalation route (MTX-LDH), and its hematocompatibility was investigated. Hemolysis, a red blood cell counting assay, and optical microscopy revealed that the MTX-LDH had no harmful toxic effect on blood cells.

pmc-10670313.title: Mechanisms of Endothelial Cell Membrane Repair: Progress and Perspectives
pmc-10670313.creator: Duoduo Zha, Shizhen Wang, Paula Monaghan-Nichols, Yisong Qian, Venkatesh Sampath, Mingui Fu
pmc-10670313.description: Endothelial cells are the crucial inner lining of blood vessels, which are pivotal in vascular homeostasis and integrity. However, these cells are perpetually subjected to a myriad of mechanical, chemical, and biological stresses that can compromise their plasma membranes. A sophisticated repair system involving key molecules, such as calcium, annexins, dysferlin, and MG53, is essential for maintaining endothelial viability.

pmc-11613175.title: IFRD1 is required for maintenance of bladder epithelial homeostasis
pmc-11613175.creator: Bisiayo E. Fashemi, Amala K. Rougeau, Arnold M. Salazar, Steven J. Bark, Rayvanth Chappidi, Jeffrey W. Brown, Charles J. Cho, Jason C. Mills, Indira U. Mysorekar
pmc-11613175.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). SummaryThe maintenance of homeostasis and rapid regeneration of the urothelium following stress are critical for bladder function. Here, we identify a key role for IFRD1 in maintaining urothelial homeostasis in a mouse model. We demonstrate that the murine bladder expresses IFRD1 at homeostasis, particularly in the urothelium, and its loss alters the global transcriptome with significant accumulation of endolysosomes and dysregulated uroplakin expression pattern. We show that IFRD1 interacts with mRNA-translation-regulating factors in human urothelial cells.

pmc-12687656.title: Neuromuscular Mechanisms of Motor Adaptation to Repeated Treadmill-Slip Perturbations During Stance in Healthy Young Adults
pmc-12687656.creator: Shuaijie Wang, Rudri Purohit, Tamaya Van Criekinge, Tanvi Bhatt
pmc-12687656.description: Treadmill-based repeated perturbation training (PBT) induces motor adaptation in reactive balance responses, thus lowering the risk of slip-induced falls. However, little evidence exists regarding intervention-induced changes in neuromuscular control underlying motor adaptation. Examining neuromuscular changes could be an important step in identifying key elements of adaptation and evaluating treadmill training protocols for fall prevention.
